newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Embattled P&U pins hopes on new boss.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Embattled P&U pins hopes on new boss.

text.p: The embattled Swedish-American drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) was hoping it had started to turn the corner on Sunday with the appointment of a new chief executive officer. The company said 51-year old Fred Hassan, poached from P&U's much larger rival American Home Products Corp "was exactly the right person to lead Pharmacia & Upjohn into the 21st century." Analysts described Hassan as a trouble-shooter who had the business and scientific skills to reverse the fortunes of P&U, which has been rocked by falling profits and the departure in January of former chief executive John Zabriskie. "This should stabilise the share price and bring confidence back to investors," said Goldman Sachs analyst Prem Lachman.

Hassan, an American of Pakistani origin, was executive vice president at AHP. He is credited with masterminding AHP's merger with American Cynamid, and P&U was also keen to stress his international experience and his background in the key field of research and development (R&D). He will start work at the group's international headquarters in Windsor, England, on Monday.

Hassan's appointment should end the sense of instability which has plagued P&U in recent months following Zabriskie's resignation and a spate of profit warnings, which culminated in a sharp decline in first-quarter earnings and sales.

Shares in the group, which merged in November 1995, have retreated steadily, dropping from 273 Swedish crowns and $39.88 at the start of the year to lows of 217 crowns and $27.50 in April. They closed at 243.5 crowns in Stockholm on Friday and at $32.00 in New York. Analysts have criticised the company for failing to meet targets on cost-savings and profits. Zabriskie was believed to have been forced out because of differences over the pace of cost-cutting. The appointment of Hassan should reassure analysts, who were keen to see a strong figure at the helm. He has 26 years of experience behind him and headed Swiss group Sandoz's U.S. pharmaceuticals and R&D operations before joining AHP in 1989. From November 1995 Hassan was in charge of AHP's world-wide pharmaceutical, medical device and nutrition businesses as well as its R&D. Goldman Sachs's Lachman said "this is what we have been looking for - a capable, R&D-learned individual who can turn this company around." Lachman said

His first task will be to build something of substance out of the rather wishy-washy recovery strategy unveiled by P&U last month, which included refocusing its drug portfolio and boosting spending on new product launches. He will also be keen to stamp his authority on the company after continued speculation over disagreements at the top. Jan Ekberg, who will resume the role of chairman after filling in for Zabriskie, told reporters Hassan would be given a free hand to change the recovery strategy and would be "fully responsible for the whole company to the board."
